correctness.rationale: The proof is an exact matrix-equivalence argument. Since \(P\) is a permutation matrix, \((A\otimes P)(I_n\otimes P^T)=A\otimes I_m\); a perfect shuffle turns this into \(I_m\otimes A\). Column permutations preserve the code up to coordinate relabeling and row permutations preserve its kernel, yielding \(C^{\oplus m}\). The enumerator, minimum-distance, dimension, connected-component, and cycle-count consequences are immediate invariants of a direct sum/disjoint union. The bundled finite replay checks the published \([12,2,8]\) example and every one of the \(64\) lifted words.

value.rationale: The source presents the Kronecker construction as a way to generate larger LDPC codes and studies Tanner-graph features such as girth and absorbing sets. The decomposition shows that the uniform version cannot create new connected Tanner topology: it merely replicates the base constituent. This exactly characterizes its full weight distribution and cycle multiplicities and clarifies why the source's position-dependent permutation generalization is the mathematically meaningful route to genuinely mixed lifts.
